title: Protocol to analyze antitumor immunity of orthotopic injection and spontaneous murine high-grade glioma models using flow cytometry and single-cell RNA sequencing
protocol: Anesthetize pups via hypothermia by placing them on ice for at least 5 min.
Mix plasmid DNA solution with Fast Green.
Remove tip from micropipette.
Connect micropipette with a silicon tube.
Load micropipette tip with the plasmid DNA solution.
Inject plasmid DNA into the lateral ventricle at approximately 1/3 the length of the virtual line between the right eye and lambda.
Confirm plasmid DNA injection into the lateral ventricle via illumination.
Transfect plasmid DNA into the brain via electroporation using a Tweezer electrode.
Prepare sgRNA-Trp53/Pten-Cas9-Cre plasmid DNA inserted into the brain of 0–2-day-old pups.
Dilute plasmid DNA stock to 2 μg/μL in ddH2O.
Add Fast green (10% final volume) to plasmid DNA solution.
Prepare a piece of parafilm to place several droplets (1 μL per droplet) of plasmid DNA solution.
Slightly cut off the tip of a micropipette using forceps before loading the droplet.
Connect the other side of a micropipette to a silicon tube for blowing out the DNA.
Bring the micropipette tip to the droplet and roll it until the droplet is completely loaded.
Inject the plasmid DNA into the lateral ventricle of the brain.
Make a virtual line between the right eye and lambda.
Make the insertion point at about 1/3 the length of this line from the lambda.
Insert the micropipette tip into this position at a depth of 2 μm from the skull.
Extrude the DNA by blowing the other side of the silicon tube.
Confirm the injection using Fast Green to show the shape of the lateral ventricle.
Prepare an electroporator and a tweezer electrode.
Set the pulse condition to 100 V, 50 ms with intervals of 950 ms for 5 pulses.
Soak the electrode tips with PBS.
Hold the brain with the wet electrode.
Apply the electric pulses; positive electrode ahead of the eye, negative on the ventricle side opposite.
Return the pups to the cage after injection.
Prepare the mouse for stereotaxic surgery.
Anesthetize a mouse with isoflurane.
Turn on a heating pad.
Fix the mouse on a stereotaxic instrument that connects to an anesthesia machine administering isoflurane.
Arrange the insertion position.
Sterilize the skin of the head.
Cut the skin along the midline of the head (∼1 cm) with a surgical scissor.
Peel off the mucus on the skull with a cotton swab.
Fix a sterile pen on the syringe holder and mark locations starting from bregma as zero for the x- and y-axes.
Mark another location 2.0 mm anterior and 2.0 mm right of bregma.
Fix the mouse on a stereotaxic instrument for brain tumor injection.
Drill a hole in the skull at 2.0 mm anterior and 2.0 mm right from the bregma of the brain.
Load a Hamilton syringe with prepared GL261 cells in a volume of 2 μL.
Move the syringe to the drilled hole and touch the needle tip to the tissue surface.
Set the needle position as zero for the z-axis.
Move the syringe down to 3.5 mm inferior from the brain surface.
Wait for 1 min after reaching the injection depth.
Move the syringe up to 0.5 mm superior (3.0 mm inferior from the surface).
Inject GL261 cells at a rate of 0.4 μL/min for 5 min with a syringe infusion pump.
Remove the syringe carefully and slowly after injection.
Fill the hole with bonding material mixed with beads.
Tighten the skin around the wound with surgical suture thread.
Place the mouse back into its cage post-procedure.
Place the mouse onto the surgery area and fix it in position.
Incise the ventral side of the skin and snip the thoracic cavity carefully.
Pin both sides of the ribs to create space for needle injection into the heart.
Insert the syringe needle containing PBS into the left ventricle and make a small hole in the right atrium.
Push the syringe plunger with moderate force to perfuse the system.
Confirm that the liver's redness has faded after perfusion.
Harvest the brain tissue from the mouse.
Cut the skin of the head along the midline from the neck to the eyes.
Hold the skin open on both sides and cut the skull along the sagittal suture starting from the brainstem.
Remove both halves of the skull carefully without damaging the brain tissue.
Pull out the brain and place it into cold DMEM.
Prepare an enzyme mixture containing 2 mg/mL Collagenase IV and 30 μg/mL DNase I in 5 mL of isolation buffer.
Sterilize a razor with 100% ethanol.
Place the brain tissue on a 60-mm petri dish and chop it finely using the sterilized razor.
Transfer the chopped tissue pieces into a new 15-mL tube containing 5 mL of enzyme mixture, being careful not to block the pipette end.
Incubate the tissue in a shaking water bath at 37°C for 30 minutes.
Incubate the tube at 4°C, 440 rcf for 5 minutes.
Remove the supernatant and resuspend the pellet with 5 mL of dissociation buffer.
Incubate at 37°C for 5 minutes in a shaking water bath.
Dissociate cells from the tissue suspension.
Prepare a 60-mm petri dish, a syringe plunger, and a 70-μm strainer.
Place the strainer on the petri dish.
Vortex the tissue suspension thoroughly and pour it into the strainer.
Grind the tissue with the syringe plunger thoroughly.
Wash the strainer with 5 mL of isolation buffer.
Transfer the homogenate from the strainer to a new 15-mL tube.
Repeat washing and transfer the homogenate to a new tube.
Centrifuge the tube at 4°C, 440 rcf for 5 minutes.
Remove the supernatant of the centrifuged homogenate.
Resuspend the pellet with 5 mL of 30% Percoll solution.
Place a Pasteur pipette into the tube.
Add 3 mL of 70% Percoll solution below the 30% Percoll solution through the Pasteur pipette.
Centrifuge the tube at room temperature, 800 rcf for 20 minutes.
Remove the myelin debris on the 70% Percoll layer.
Take approximately 3 mL of media from the line between the 30% and 70% Percoll layers.
Transfer into a new 15-mL tube.
Add FACS buffer to a total volume of 15 mL and invert gently.
Centrifuge the tube at 4°C, 440 rcf for 5 minutes.
Remove red blood cells by ACK lysis buffer.
Remove the supernatant.
Resuspend the cell pellet with 1 mL of ACK lysis buffer, and incubate at RT for 5 min.
Add 1 mL of FACS buffer, and centrifuge at 4°C, 440 rcf for 5 min.
Remove the supernatant and resuspend the cell pellet with 1 mL of RPMI CM.
Filter cells with a sterilized 70-μm mesh.
Count the number of cells using trypan blue and a cell counter.
Transfer an adequate amount of cells into a 5-mL round-bottom polystyrene tube.
Centrifuge the tube at 4°C, 440 rcf for 5 min.
Remove the supernatant and add 100 μL (per million cells) of Fc block diluted in FACS buffer to a 1:100 ratio.
Incubate on ice for 20 min in the dark.
Add 1 mL of FACS buffer to the sample.
Centrifuge at 4°C, 440 rcf for 5 min.
Remove the supernatant and add 100 μL (per million cells) of anti-CD45 antibody diluted in FACS buffer at a 1:200 ratio.
Incubate the sample on ice for 30 min in the dark.
Add 1 mL of FACS buffer to the sample.
Centrifuge at 4°C, 440 rcf for 5 min.
Remove the supernatant and resuspend the cell pellet in 1–2 mL of FACS buffer.
Add 5 μL (per million cells) of 7-AAD and incubate for 5–10 min in the dark prior to flow sorting.
Sort ∼1–2 × 10^5 7-AAD-CD45+ immune cells using the FACS Aria II into a new 15-mL tube containing RPMI CM.
Centrifuge at 4°C, 440 rcf for 5 min and remove the supernatant being careful not to touch the cell pellet.
Resuspend the cell pellet with cold PBS to a concentration of 700–1200 cells/μL.
Prepare a master mix for barcoding that contains RT Reagent, Template Switch Oligo, Reducing Agent B, and RT Enzyme C.
Install a Chromium Chip B in a 10× Chip Holder and add 50% glycerol solution into the unused chip wells (row #1: 75 μL, row #2: 40 μL, row #3: 280 μL).
Vortex Gel Bead strip for 30 seconds in a 10× Vortex Adaptor.
Mix cell suspension with the corresponding volume of master mix for barcoding.
Load the mixture onto the Chromium Chip without introducing bubbles.
Attach the 10× Gasket to the Chromium Chip and place it in the tray of the Controller.
Start the Chromium Single Cell B program.
Transfer 100 μL of gel-based emulsions (GEMs) from the Recovery wells into a tube strip on ice.
Incubate at 53°C for 45 minutes.
Incubate at 85°C for 5 minutes.
Hold sample at 4°C.
Purify first-strand cDNA from the reaction mixture.
Add 125 μL of Recovery Agent to each sample at room temperature without pipette mixing or vortexing.
Wait 60 seconds after adding Recovery Agent.
Carefully remove 125 μL of Recovery Agent/Partitioning Oil from the bottom.
Thoroughly mix Dynabeads MyOne SILANE by vortexing before use.
Add 200 μL of Dynabeads Cleanup Mix to each sample.
Mix by pipetting.
Incubate for 10 min at room temperature (RT).
Mix again at approximately 5 min after the start of incubation by pipetting.
During the incubation, prepare Elution Solution I containing elution buffer, 10% Tween-20, and Reducing Agent B with vortexing and spin down.
After incubation, place the sample on the High position of a 10× Magnetic Separator until the solution clears.
Remove the supernatant.
Wash twice with 80% ethanol.
Place the sample on the Low position of the separator.
Remove the remaining ethanol by air drying for 1 min.
Remove the sample from the separator.
Add 35.5 μL of Elution Solution I to each sample.
Incubate for 2 min at RT.
Place the sample on the Low position of the separator until the solution clears.
Transfer 35 μL of the sample into a new tube strip.
Amplify the cDNA with Amp Mix and cDNA primers using a thermal cycler programmed with the specified protocol.
Clean up cDNA using SPRIselect.
Add SPRIselect reagent (0.6×) to each sample.
Incubate for 5 min at RT.
Place on the High position of the separator until the solution clears.
Remove the supernatant.
Wash twice with 80% ethanol.
Place the sample on the Low position of the separator.
Remove the remaining ethanol by air drying for 2 min.
Remove the sample from the separator.
Elute with elution buffer for 2 min at room temperature.
Place the sample on the High position of the separator until the solution clears.
Transfer 40 μL of sample into a new tube strip.
Dilute 1 μL of sample at a 1:10 ratio using distilled water.
Use the Agilent High Sensitivity DNA Kit with Agilent 2100 Bioanalyzer for quantification.
Hold at 4°C for 5 min.
Incubate at 32°C for 5 min.
Incubate at 65°C for 30 min.
Hold at 4°C.
Add Fragmentation Buffer and Fragmentation Enzyme to the sample.
Clean up the sample using SPRIselect reagent.
Add 30 μL of 0.6× SPRIselect reagent to each sample.
Incubate at room temperature for 5 min.
Place on the High position of the separator until the solution clears.
Transfer 75 μL of supernatant to a new tube strip.
Add 10 μL of 0.8× SPRIselect reagent to each sample.
Incubate at room temperature for 5 min.
Place the solution on the High position of the separator until it clears.
Remove the supernatant and wash twice with 80% ethanol.
Elute the sample with elution buffer for 2 minutes at room temperature (RT).
Incubate each sample with a mix containing Ligation Buffer, DNA Ligase, and Adaptor Oligos in a thermal cycler: 15 minutes at 20°C followed by holding at 4°C.
Repeat the clean-up process using 0.8× SPRIselect reagent and the separator.
Incubate each sample with a PCR mix containing Amp Mix, SI Primer, and an individual Chromium i7 Sample Index on a thermal cycler according to the inputted amount of cDNA.
Repeat the clean-up process using 0.6× SPRIselect reagent and the separator.
Dilute 1 μL of sample at a 1:10 ratio with DW.
Use the Agilent High Sensitivity DNA Kit with Agilent 2100 Bioanalyzer to assess library construction quality.

Sequence the library using the Illumina HiSeq X Ten sequencing system with the HiSeq X Ten Reagent Kit v2.5 and PhiX Control v3 according to recommended cycle conditions: Read 1 - 28 cycles, i7 index - 8 cycles, i5 index - unspecified cycles, and Read 2 - 91 cycles.
Use Chromium Cell Ranger to generate bacords.tsv, features.tsv, and matrix.mtx files for sequencing data.
Read sequencing data using the Read10X function.
Create Seurat objects using the CreateSeuratObject function.
Check the level of nFeature_RNA, nCount_RNA, and mitochondrial gene expression in samples.
Isolate quality-controlled objects using the Subset function.
Normalize data using the NormalizeData function.
Identify variable features in objects using the FindVariableFeatures function.
Combine objects for further analysis.
Find anchorsets among combined objects using the FindIntegrationAnchors function.
Integrate datasets using the IntegrateData function.
Cluster and visualize the data to understand cellular heterogeneity.
Scale features in the dataset using the ScaleData function.
Set “integrated” as a default assay in Seurat objects.
Reduce dataset dimension using the RunPCA function.
Further reduce dataset complexity using the RunUMAP function.
Construct a shared nearest neighbor graph from the dataset using the FindNeighbors function.
Identify clusters of cells by shared nearest neighbors using the FindClusters function.
Visualize identified clusters using the DimPlot function.
Transfer 1 × 10^6 cells from each sample to a new 5-mL polystyrene tube.
Centrifuge the tube at 4°C, 440 rcf for 5 min.
Remove the supernatant and add 100 μL (per million cells) of Fc block diluted in FACS buffer at a 1:100 ratio.
Incubate on ice for 20 min in the dark.
Add 1 mL of FACS buffer to the sample and centrifuge at 4°C, 440 rcf for 5 min.
Remove the supernatant and add 100 μL (per million cells) of antibody mixture.
Incubate on ice for 30 min in the dark.
Add 1 mL of FACS buffer to the sample and centrifuge at 4°C, 440 rcf for 5 min.
Repeat this step once.
Remove the supernatant and resuspend the cell pellet in 300 μL of FACS buffer.
Before analysis, add 5 μL of propidium iodide solution to the sample.
Incubate for 5 min.
Acquire cells using the FACS Fortessa X-20 machine (or other flow cytometer).
Export .fcs data and load to FlowJo (or other software) for analysis.
Identify cell types using cell lineage markers.
